analysis: Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a paragraph after head line 783 saying provider-staged complete-checkpoint imports create destinations already available from host bytes, evaluate or fence nothing, and so never wait on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock held during another request's prefill chunk. It also says the import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift). No code or controls changed in the supplied evidence, so there is no direct regression. Relevant threats: T-041 (prefix-cache cross-tenant TTFT oracle and SSD at-rest posture), T-010 and T-029 (availability), and A-001. This is a described behavioural change in the unseen implementation: staging no longer blocks on evalLock. It could slightly change hit/miss timing and the TTFT oracle in T-041, and it affects memory-accounting claims. The implementation is not in this batch, so I cannot verify that the claim matches the code. Items the next pass should check: (1) that the real CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift still authenticates the full file before any host-backed destination becomes usable; (2) that the host-zero scratch charge is bounded in the admission ledger; (3) that the T-041 sign-off is not invalidated by the timing change. No threat-model assets, trust boundaries or mitigations are contradicted by the doc text itself.
